expect.note: the opt-in expect keys are carried by exactly the cases the docs name; and a run that ends BEFORE grading reports its status against the expectation for every `expect` shape that implies verdict PASS, instead of subscripting a None verdict

provenance: two `expect` keys exist so a case can say something the harness cannot infer — `mutation_survived: false` (this run succeeded and is still not a survival) and `answer_is_known_wrong: true` (this expectation pins the wrong answer as ground truth). Both are described in prose across ADR-009, docs/support-matrix.md and docs/evals/evaluation-methodology.md, and that prose has already gone stale once: after round 2 removed the key from l4-shop-render-delayed (its status excludes it now), the methodology doc still said the key kept BOTH non-survivors out of the numerator, for a whole review round (PR #12, R12). Sets rather than counts, so a mismatch names the file that moved. Watched red by adding `mutation_survived` to a second case: the check reports declared ['l4-shop-element-reordered'] vs actual two ids. M31 and PR #29 added three more, each for the same reason — the harness cannot infer them from a run: `actions` (a plan rejected before the browser moved spends exactly the pre-plan navigation), `planner_note_contains` (WHICH replan prompt a path sends, since the stub planner discards the note) and `trace_note_contains` (that the trace records why a plan changed). M28 added three more for the shape of a verifier-rejected run, which no status/verdict key can see: `answer_null` (the demoted run carries no answer), `reason_max_chars` (the reason does not quote the rejected dump back) and `evidence_contains` (the extraction is still in evidence, in full). T-M40-2 adds no key: `plan-lint-refuses-a-document-root-extract` reuses `actions`, `planner_note_contains` and `answer_null` — a plan refused before execution is the shape all three were written for — and is declared against each of them here; its mid-run twin (PR #46 R1) reuses `answer_null` and nothing else new. M38 added three cases to `trace_note_contains` rather than a fourth key: WHICH narrowing rung settled an ambiguity is exactly the 'why did this step do that' the trace note already carries, and a run that answered from one of several matches without saying which rung picked it is the reading M38's ADR-026 refuses. M43 (ADR-035) adds three keys of the same opt-in kind and declares them here from birth: `trace_screenshots` (screenshot-per-trace-step, as booleans in step order), `driver_screenshots` (what image frame each driver call's observation actually carried, verified against the PNG file at call time), and `trace_values` (the `value` recorded on a named trace step — how a coordinate click's coordinates are asserted without a schema change). Extended 2026-08-28 to grade the OTHER registry in the same file, closing T-R83: `KINDS` carried `"readyz-transitions": _run_readyz_case` twice. Both entries named the same handler so nothing misbehaved, which is exactly why it sat there for a milestone — the next duplicate is two entries pointing at DIFFERENT handlers, silently last-wins, with the losing case running the wrong grader and no error anywhere. It is graded here rather than in a case of its own because it is the same property this case already grades: a registry key that decides which grader runs. The check parses the SOURCE with `ast` — a dict literal cannot be asked about duplicates at runtime, since by the time it exists the loser is gone. Watched red by re-introducing the duplicate: `{registry: KINDS, duplicate_keys: [readyz-transitions]}`. T-M32-11 (P2) closed here 2026-08-28. `_run_fixture_case` evaluated `result["verdict"]["verdict"]` whenever `audit["layer"] == 1`, and `result["verdict"]` is None for any run that ends before grading — every refusal path and every `failure:*` exit. `want_verdict` is truthy whenever `expect` OMITS `status`, sets `status: success`, or names a verdict outright, i.e. for most cases. The subscript raised `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable` and the case reported a traceback instead of the failure it had just produced, turning "the run failed loudly" into "the harness broke". All three shapes are probed — `{}`, `{status: success}`, `{verdict: PASS}` — because the block's acceptance says in as many words that it must not be closable by special-casing the empty one. It is graded here rather than in a new case for the reason the KINDS duplicate is: this case already grades what the harness does with a registry and a declaration it cannot satisfy. Found live, not from the block: widening `_AGGREGATE` for T-CHEAPEST-WORDING flipped `verifier-precision-recall` onto a verdictless path and the adapter crashed exactly as described.

triage.note: guards a documentation claim, not the product — the same shape as support-matrix-cites-real-cases and the MUTATIONS coverage check in mutation-catalog-integrity. Also refuses `answer_is_known_wrong` on a case with no `expect.answer`, where the marker would label nothing.

provenance_m42_2026_08_26: M42 adds `loop-refuses-a-document-root-extract` to the `trace_note_contains` list. The key carries the same weight there it carries everywhere else — it is the only thing that can see a refusal the run then RECOVERED from, which is the whole shape of the re-homed ADR-024 guard in loop mode: the run ends `success`, so the status says nothing about whether the root read was refused or quietly allowed.
provenance_m46_2026_08_28: M46 (ADR-037) adds two. `legs` is a per-leg subset match on an escalate run's `legs` array — mode, status, step count and each leg's own budgets — and nothing else can see whether the escalation FIRED, because a one-leg and a two-leg escalate run reach the same statuses. `driver_note_lacks` is the negative half of `driver_note_contains` and exists for one case: the seeded note is a channel from the plan leg's page-derived evidence into the loop driver's prompt, and asserting what a note CONTAINS can never show that a payload did not ride along with it. Declaring it here is not bookkeeping: a misspelled negative assertion is silently green, and a security case that is silently green reads as proof that an injection channel is closed when nothing was tested. PR #78 R1 adds `escalate-refuses-after-a-completed-state-change` to `legs` and to `answer_null`: the refusal to escalate past a completed state change is visible ONLY as a one-entry `legs` array on a run whose statuses would otherwise look identical to a loop leg that never started. PR #78 R8 adds the other two postcondition branches — `escalate-refuses-after-a-failed-postcondition` (the `false` cell) and `escalate-refuses-after-an-unverified-state-change` (the `null` cell) — to `legs` and `answer_null`, so all three branches of the refusal are declared together and one of them going missing is red rather than quiet.
provenance_pr60_2026_08_27: PR #60 R4 adds `max_ms`, the first expect key that is an upper BOUND rather than an equality: `budgets` compares exactly and a duration is never equal twice, so the cost half of a finding whose correctness half was already green had nothing to be written in. R1 adds `resolver-case-fold-is-recorded-in-the-trace` to `trace_note_contains` — a name matched case-insensitively is a looser reading of what the plan asked for, and which reading was used is the same 'why did this step do that' the note already carries for M38's rungs.
provenance_pr60_r3_2026_08_27: PR #60 R15 adds `resolver-narrowing-discloses-the-case-fold`: a resolution that used BOTH an M38 rung and the T-M42-20 case-fold reported only the rung, so the note is now every relaxation joined and this case is what pins the composed form. `trace_note_contains` is a substring test, so the four rung cases already carrying it are byte-identical.
provenance_pr70_r9_2026_08_28: PR #70 R9 adds `loop-drill-capture-does-not-scroll-the-page`, the first case to use `false` in a `driver_screenshots` list: the assertion is that a drill whose target lies outside the viewport carries NO crop at all, with the turns either side keeping their viewport frames. Without it the case pinned only the answer, so a build that dropped element crops entirely — or emitted one for an off-screen element by scrolling to it — shipped green on a case written to catch exactly that.
